correctness.rationale: Tame cyclic degree-five cover with four simple branch points has genus four; valuations yield an explicit basis of four regular differentials. The characteristic-three Cartier rule gives \(\mathcal C(e_1)=\lambda^{2/3}e_3+(1+\lambda)^{1/3}e_4\), \(\mathcal C(e_2)=0\), \(\mathcal C(e_3)=-(1+\lambda)^{1/3}e_2\), and \(\mathcal C(e_4)=\lambda^{1/3}e_2\). Thus \(\operatorname{rank}\mathcal C=2\), \(\mathcal C^3=0\), and the ninth power of the unique coefficient of \(\mathcal C^2\) is \(-\lambda^2(1+\lambda)(\lambda-1)^2\), vanishing for smooth parameters precisely at \(\lambda=-1\). Symbolic polynomial algebra and exhaustive finite-field checks of orders 3, 9, 27 are replayable in the embedded source; finite enumeration is a check, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The \(M[11]\) genus-four one-dimensional special family is a natural object of arithmetic geometry. Its characteristic-three exact Cartier-square jumping locus is a complete geometric stratification rather than an arbitrary parameter test, and the jump at the uniquely symmetric branch configuration distinguishes nilpotence indices even though both \(3\)-rank and \(a\)-number remain constant. This is a motivated, non-implied exact boundary relevant to comparisons of Frobenius structures in positive-characteristic families.
